a122.speaker: Government of Liberia
a122.name: Government of Liberia
a122.speech: Says it will fully support the National AIDS Commission (NAC) to ensure that it carries out its statutory mandate.

a122.speaker: Jerolinmek Piah, Information Minister of Liberia
a122.name: Jerolinmek Piah
a122.title: Information Minister of Liberia
a122.speech: Noted that the government will do all it can to ensure that people living with HIV are not at risk ; “The government will work with the Commission to provide people living with the virus their medication and other supplements.”

a122.speaker: Jerolinmek Piah, Information Minister of Liberia
a122.name: Jerolinmek Piah
a122.title: Information Minister of Liberia
a122.speech: Speaking at the MICAT Regular Press Briefing in Monrovia, stressed that the government is taking the necessary steps to address the issues that have to do with USAID ; indicated that the measure has to do with waste in terms of the government’s financial activities across all sectors.

a144.speaker: Professor Prabhakaran Paleri, retired Director General of the Indian Coast Guard
a144.name: Professor Prabhakaran Paleri
a144.title: retired Director General of the Indian Coast Guard
a144.speech: His holistic framework of 33 elements of national security including human well-being, governance, cyber threats and environmental security offered an expansive view far beyond conventional military lenses.

a150.speaker: Galmudug security officials
a150.name: Galmudug security officials
a150.speech: According to them, the death toll from the clan fight that erupted in central Somalia has risen to 50, with over 80 reported injured.

a150.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Abdiasis Ibrahim Adan, Galmudug’s deputy police commissioner
a150.name: Lieutenant Colonel Abdiasis Ibrahim Adan
a150.title: Galmudug’s deputy police commissioner
a150.speech: “Since yesterday, we have tried to cease the fighting. The rival militia are still in their positions and we have not managed to remove them” ; “We have collected about 50 bodies and recovered the injured. We estimate between 80 to 90. We have handed them to their families” ; “They are very armed. You know all clans have heavy weaponry which they got to strengthen during recent military operations.”

a150.speaker: Journalists and officials
a150.name: Journalists and officials
a150.speech: Have reported that the conflict, involving militias from the Mareexaan and Dir clans, stems from an old dispute over the ownership of a water well and surrounding rural villages.

a150.speaker: Galmudug authorities
a150.name: Galmudug authorities
a150.speech: Have announced plans to send officials, clan elders, and religious leaders to the area in an attempt to mediate and bring about peace.

a150.speaker: Mohamed Abdi Adan, Galmudug internal security minister
a150.name: Mohamed Abdi Adan
a150.title: Galmudug internal security minister
a150.speech: “I am very sorry for the renewed war in the Landheer area. It is not expected today; it is not irreversible. The president has already spoken about it and called for peace.”

a150.speaker: Witnesses
a150.name: Witnesses
a150.speech: Reported that bodies of the deceased lay at the scene until Saturday afternoon.

a150.speaker: One faction involved in the conflict
a150.name: One faction involved in the conflict
a150.speech: Claimed to have closed the Caabudwaaq airport, a critical facility that handles daily domestic flights from Mogadishu.

a150.speaker: Sources (anonymous)
a150.name: Sources (anonymous)
a150.speech: Indicated that there is a substantial risk if the warring militias, who possess anti-aircraft weapons, target civilian flights.

a150.speaker: Religious scholars in Cadaado
a150.name: Religious scholars in Cadaado
a150.speech: Have called for an immediate halt to the fighting and urged the Galmudug administration to take decisive action to end the conflict.

a150.speaker: Abdi Omar, religious cleric
a150.name: Abdi Omar
a150.title: religious cleric
a150.speech: “It is unfortunate and has caused heavy losses.”

a150.speaker: Local police
a150.name: Local police
a150.speech: Have urged President Ahmed Qoorqoor of Galmudug, clan elders, and religious men to intervene swiftly to prevent further bloodshed and foster dialogue between the conflicting parties.

a214.speaker: Marthe Coulibaly, national coordinator of the Ivorian Coalition of Human Rights Defenders (CIDDH)
a214.name: Marthe Coulibaly
a214.title: national coordinator of the Ivorian Coalition of Human Rights Defenders (CIDDH)
a214.speech: Stated in her intervention that this is a project which started in 2021 and is continuing. It is aimed at women but also at young girls in order to prepare them to understand the issues of community development. Several activities are on the programme: capacity-building of the project's beneficiaries in terms of leadership and advocacy, so that social and societal responsibility is respected.

a214.speaker: Marthe Coulibaly, national coordinator of the Ivorian Coalition of Human Rights Defenders (CIDDH)
a214.name: Marthe Coulibaly
a214.title: national coordinator of the Ivorian Coalition of Human Rights Defenders (CIDDH)
a214.speech: Indicated that the expectations of the NGOs towards the AfDB are enormous: "The NGOs are the ones on the ground who relay the concerns of the communities. That is why we expect our recommendations to be taken into account at these meetings."

a428.speaker: Maryan Nur Mohamed, displaced mother of eight at Hilac-Wanaag camp, Garasbaley district, Mogadishu
a428.name: Maryan Nur Mohamed
a428.title: displaced mother of eight at Hilac-Wanaag camp, Garasbaley district, Mogadishu
a428.speech: "We all have nothing to eat. We don't have food. We can't find a thousand Somali shillings to buy food. We beg for food and everything else. We ran away from that war and brought our children here with whatever we could carry. We joined this camp and we are here now – that's how it is."

a428.speaker: Maryan Nur Mohamed, displaced mother of eight at Hilac-Wanaag camp, Garasbaley district, Mogadishu
a428.name: Maryan Nur Mohamed
a428.title: displaced mother of eight at Hilac-Wanaag camp, Garasbaley district, Mogadishu
a428.speech: On conditions in the camp and life before displacement: "We put mats on the floor that we received from people around the camp. They also help us with a few bottles of water shared by everyone in the hall, about 100 families. We had a good life back home, but now we are in a difficult situation. In the past, we used to work on farms and eat whatever we could find. We cooked grains and harvested vegetables. We came to this camp to live among other people. We passed through many places as we were running from the war, so we don't know who is dead or alive."

a428.speaker: Maryan Nur Mohamed, displaced mother of eight at Hilac-Wanaag camp, Garasbaley district, Mogadishu
a428.name: Maryan Nur Mohamed
a428.title: displaced mother of eight at Hilac-Wanaag camp, Garasbaley district, Mogadishu
a428.speech: On the farm and livestock she lost: "We fled from the fields when the crops were about to be harvested. The goats were left behind because we couldn't bring them to Mogadishu." ; on the sudden eruption of violence: "The shelling started suddenly. When we could no longer bear it, we were forced to run for our lives. A local businessman helped us escape in his car."

a428.speaker: Fowsiya Abukar Ali, displaced mother of 11 at Hilaac IDP camp
a428.name: Fowsiya Abukar Ali
a428.title: displaced mother of 11 at Hilaac IDP camp
a428.speech: "Those who came before us only get a small amount of food. When they get nothing, they sleep hungry… The poor economy in the camp and the lack of food mean my children cry with hunger and still have nothing to eat." ; "I swear to God that I can't find food right now as I speak to you, unless someone gives me something to eat. Otherwise, I only drink water as food. I don't have anything else. I only depend on God. We don't have a place to live. People can't live together in one place. We don't have a house, we don't have anything to eat, not even utensils to cook with." ; "We are sleeping outside and have no hope of returning home, as the fighting is still going on there."

a428.speaker: Fowsiya Abukar Ali, displaced mother of 11 at Hilaac IDP camp
a428.name: Fowsiya Abukar Ali
a428.title: displaced mother of 11 at Hilaac IDP camp
a428.speech: Described how a farm where her relatives gathered was bombed from the air: "We decided to flee the area rather than end up dead. The plane was not visible, and the people we were looking for were hiding among others. When the missile fell, it hit the people in the fields. It was thought to be Al-Shabaab, and that's how the attack happened. Three of my brothers were killed." ; on her husband, who stayed behind to protect their twice-bombed farm: "He has no money to follow us here. I have no relatives in Hamar [Mogadishu] to support me, and he can't help. My children and I suffer from the sun during the day and the cold at night. The children can't sleep at night because of the cold."

a428.speaker: Maymun Mahmoud Yusuf, displaced mother of three from Bushra Sheikh area in Adale
a428.name: Maymun Mahmoud Yusuf
a428.title: displaced mother of three from Bushra Sheikh area in Adale
a428.speech: Told Radio Ergo that life in the camp is harder than anything she has experienced before: "The war destroyed our hut house. I took the children without carrying anything for them. While we stood on the road, a relative put us in a car. That's how we got to Mogadishu." ; "We have no money. We came here with hardship and suffering. My children and I are very poor. We live on what people collect for us. Sometimes we don't get it, sometimes we do, usually only once a day."

a428.speaker: Mohamed Aweys Mohamed, community member helping displaced families
a428.name: Mohamed Aweys Mohamed
a428.title: community member helping displaced families
a428.speech: Said about 1,500 families were distributed into 15 different camps, of which 300 went to Hilac-Wanaag camp in Garasbaley district: "They could not afford houses, so we built a corrugated iron hall to protect them from the sun during the day." ; "I gathered the neighbours and asked who could donate a kilo of rice, sugar, oil, or a blanket. Even those who could give 2,000 Somali shillings did. We gave what we collected to our brothers and sisters to help them."

a428.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) report
a428.name: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) report
a428.speech: According to the report, airstrikes and direct fighting in Middle Shabelle for more than a month have affected 30,000 families, including farmers, herders, and villagers, most displaced to Hiran, Banadir, and safer parts of Middle Shabelle.

a480.speaker: Aaron Motsoaledi, South African Health Minister
a480.name: Aaron Motsoaledi
a480.title: South African Health Minister
a480.speech: Said the government had still not secured any new funding for HIV after the US cut aid; denied reports that his HIV programme had been severely affected; acknowledged that there were some problems, but said it was inconceivable that South Africa's HIV programme could collapse, and accused the media of spreading a negative message.

a480.speaker: Aaron Motsoaledi, South African Health Minister
a480.name: Aaron Motsoaledi
a480.title: South African Health Minister
a480.speech: Said US funding paid the salaries of more than 15,000 health workers, around 8,000 of whom lost their jobs; said the government had made progress with its "Close the Gap" campaign this year, putting 520,700 HIV patients on antiretroviral treatment, out of a target of 1.1 million by the end of 2025.

a480.speaker: Reuters (news agency, cited as source)
a480.name: Reuters (news agency
a480.title: cited as source)
a480.speech: Wrote that Motsoaledi said the government had not secured new HIV funding and denied reports that the programme had been severely affected; reported that HIV viral load testing had already fallen significantly in South Africa since the funding cut, a clear sign that the health system was under pressure.

a480.speaker: HIV activists
a480.name: HIV activists
a480.speech: Interrupted a parliamentary session in Cape Town on Wednesday in protest, demanding that the state implement an emergency plan; some activists questioned the figures given by the minister.

a514.speaker: Court of Appeal in Abuja
a514.name: Court of Appeal in Abuja
a514.speech: Has reaffirmed Julius Abure as the national chairman of the Labour Party (LP) as its earlier order subsists.

a514.speaker: Justice Hamma Barka, Court of Appeal
a514.name: Justice Hamma Barka
a514.title: Court of Appeal
a514.speech: In a verdict on Friday, held that the November 13, 2024 judgment, which upheld Abure as the authentic national chairman of the LP, was still subsisting, delivering judgments on two appeals, marked CA/ABJ/CV/1271/2024 filed by Senator Esther Nenadi Usman and one other, and CA/ABJ/1232/2024 filed by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and one other, with LP and others as respondents.

a514.speaker: Justice Hamma Barka, Court of Appeal
a514.name: Justice Hamma Barka
a514.title: Court of Appeal
a514.speech: In the first judgment, on the appeal by Senator Usman and another, held among others that Justice Nwite was wrong to have assumed jurisdiction over the case which related to issues about the leadership of the LP.

a514.speaker: Justice Emeka Nwite, Federal High Court, Abuja
a514.name: Justice Emeka Nwite
a514.title: Federal High Court, Abuja
a514.speech: Delivered the October 8, 2024 judgment ordering INEC to, among others, recognise and deal with the Abure-led leadership of the LP.

a563.speaker: World Food Program (U.N. food agency)
a563.name: World Food Program (U.N. food agency)
a563.speech: Announced on Friday that it is cutting food assistance for hundreds of thousands of people in Somalia; said the number of people receiving emergency food assistance in the country will decrease from 1.1 million in August to 350,000 in November due to "critical funding shortfalls" ; says it needs $98 million to "sustain a minimum of life-saving operations for 800,000 people through the lean season until March 2026."

a563.speaker: Ross Smith, the World Food Program's director of emergency preparedness and response
a563.name: Ross Smith
a563.title: the World Food Program's director of emergency preparedness and response
a563.speech: "We are seeing a dangerous rise in emergency levels of hunger, and our ability to respond is shrinking by the day." "Without urgent funding, families already pushed to the edge will be left with nothing at a time when they need it most."

a563.speaker: U.N. latest report
a563.name: U.N. latest report
a563.speech: According to the U.N.'s latest report, 4.6 million people in Somalia are facing crisis levels of hunger, and 1.8 million children are projected to suffer from acute malnutrition this year; out of these, 421,000 children are facing severe malnutrition, and the U.N. food agency has only been able to assist about 180,000.

a570.speaker: Kalahari Holdings and Footstep for Africa (the two donor companies)
a570.name: Kalahari Holdings and Footstep for Africa (the two donor companies)
a570.speech: The two companies said they became aware of the learners’ situation when it was reported in the media at the beginning of this year, and of how difficult the learners’ circumstances were, which is what led them to make an effort and support Oshamukweni school.

a570.speaker: Walde Ndevashiya, Governor of the Ohangwena Region
a570.name: Walde Ndevashiya
a570.title: Governor of the Ohangwena Region
a570.speech: In his speech said he thanked Kalahari Holdings and Footsteps for Africa for doing important work in providing money to Oshamukweni so that it can have a school hostel; said learners had been suffering because of the lack of a hostel, since they only slept in makeshift shelters of corrugated iron sheets in the school yard, while others walked very long distances to come to school.

a570.speaker: Walde Ndevashiya, Governor of the Ohangwena Region
a570.name: Walde Ndevashiya
a570.title: Governor of the Ohangwena Region
a570.speech: Warned residents of the surrounding Oshalumbo area to stop telling journalists untruths that the government is doing nothing, because this gives the government a bad image ; “My office has noted the challenges faced by the residents of Okongo constituency, such as the lack of water and of communications. Therefore, people should remain calm, because I am busy making efforts regarding the challenges you face and how they must be resolved.”

a570.speaker: Palisha Ngulu, Deputy Director of Education in the Ohangwena Region
a570.name: Palisha Ngulu
a570.title: Deputy Director of Education in the Ohangwena Region
a570.speech: Said that this is now the second time the Footsteps for Africa organisation has supported schools in Ohangwena, and that this year the organisation donated computers and a library to Nghiteke Primary School.

a570.speaker: Palisha Ngulu, Deputy Director of Education in the Ohangwena Region
a570.name: Palisha Ngulu
a570.title: Deputy Director of Education in the Ohangwena Region
a570.speech: Warned teachers to stop beating learners so much, because beating takes away a learner’s interest in coming to class; said parents should encourage their children so that they study with dedication and should keep an eye on their children’s activities at home ; “Learners, respect your teachers, keep away from smoking and alcohol, because these disturb your education.”

a570.speaker: Tuulikki Nanghelo Nelulu, representative of Kalahari Holdings
a570.name: Tuulikki Nanghelo Nelulu
a570.title: representative of Kalahari Holdings
a570.speech: Said their company aims to meet the government halfway by supporting the education sector in Namibia; said they first visited Oshamukweni school in order to carry out research on the learners’ situation, and this led them to donate money to be used to build a school hostel and a kitchen.

a578.speaker: Kano Concerned Citizens’ Initiative (KCCI), in a statement by publicity secretary Alhaji Ahmed Aminu
a578.name: Kano Concerned Citizens’ Initiative (KCCI)
a578.title: in a statement by publicity secretary Alhaji Ahmed Aminu
a578.speech: Has thrown its weight behind the move to scrutinize the operations of NGOs being funded by foreign based agencies in the state; pointed out that the urgent need to verify the motive and sources of funding of NGOs in Kano becomes pertinent considering the recent revelation of a US Congressman that alleged USAID’s funding of Boko Haram; vowed to support the special committee instituted to purge the state against global security threat; noted that the group has been following with a keen sense of responsibility the activities of various NGOs especially those with foreign connections.

a578.speaker: Kano Concerned Citizens’ Initiative (KCCI), in a statement by publicity secretary Alhaji Ahmed Aminu
a578.name: Kano Concerned Citizens’ Initiative (KCCI)
a578.title: in a statement by publicity secretary Alhaji Ahmed Aminu
a578.speech: “The recent revelation in the US Congress of the allegation of the USAID’s funding of Boko Haram raises deep concern over the activities of NGOs that have connections with foreign aid agencies. Our people are vulnerable and have become prey to exploitation by the activities of these NGOs, largely because of bad governance which has links to economic programs imposed by globalists. Our society cannot remain indifferent to all forms of exploitations and propagation of values especially on LGBTQ+ by these agents of globalists that are hostile to our Faith.”

a578.speaker: Kano Concerned Citizens’ Initiative (KCCI), in a statement by publicity secretary Alhaji Ahmed Aminu
a578.name: Kano Concerned Citizens’ Initiative (KCCI)
a578.title: in a statement by publicity secretary Alhaji Ahmed Aminu
a578.speech: “It is in this light that we welcome the move by the Kano State Government to sanitize the activities of NGOs. The high-powered Committee charged to investigate and document, sources of funding, nature of activities, areas of intervention and operational methods with a view to recommending a regulatory framework that aligns with the State’s vision and development goals. These are long overdue as Kano State should not remain an open field for testing ideas by the globalists because the State sets the pulse of entire Northern Nigeria. We commend the State Government for this bold initiative” ; the group pledged willingness to make necessary contributions towards the success of the Committee and called on all citizens of Kano State to give the Committee the support and cooperation it deserves.

a578.speaker: US Congressman (unnamed)
a578.name: US Congressman (unnamed)
a578.speech: Alleged, in a recent revelation in the US Congress, USAID’s funding of Boko Haram.

a622.speaker: General Mamadi Doumbouya, President of the Republic of Guinea (presidential decree made public on national television)
a622.name: General Mamadi Doumbouya
a622.title: President of the Republic of Guinea (presidential decree made public on national television)
a622.speech: Through a decree made public by national television on 3 March, appointed Julien Dramou, until then Adviser in charge of economic analysis at the Ministry of Transport, as the new Director-General of the Guinean Oil Palm and Rubber Company (SOGUIPAH), replacing Fode Mourana Soumah, who had been appointed in June 2022.

a645.speaker: Amnesty International
a645.name: Amnesty International
a645.speech: warns of devastating consequences as abrupt U.S. foreign aid cuts threaten human rights globally; says that given the scale of the cuts, the number and extent of robust modeling predicting substantial mortality, and the fact that deaths have been documented already, the assertion that there has not been any death stemming from these cuts defies logic.

a645.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (testimony to the US Senate and House of Representatives, May 21 and 22)
a645.name: Marco Rubio
a645.title: US Secretary of State (testimony to the US Senate and House of Representatives, May 21 and 22)
a645.speech: provided weak or incomplete answers about the grave human rights impact of the implementation of the executive order, contrary to the evidence gathered by Amnesty and other organizations, and erroneously asserted there have been no deaths associated with these cuts.

a645.speaker: Amanda Klasing, national director of government relations and advocacy with Amnesty International USA
a645.name: Amanda Klasing
a645.title: national director of government relations and advocacy with Amnesty International USA
a645.speech: “This abrupt decision and chaotic implementation by the Trump administration is reckless and profoundly damaging. The decision to cut these programs so abruptly and in this untransparent manner violates international human rights law which the U.S. is bound by and undermines decades of U.S. leadership in global humanitarian and development efforts. While U.S. funding over the decades has had a complex relationship with human rights, the scale and suddenness of these current cuts have created a life-threatening vacuum that other governments and aid organizations are not realistically able to fill in the immediate term, violating the rights to life and health, and dignity for millions.”

a645.speaker: Amanda Klasing, national director of government relations and advocacy with Amnesty International USA
a645.name: Amanda Klasing
a645.title: national director of government relations and advocacy with Amnesty International USA
a645.speech: “The right to seek safety is protected under international law which the United States is bound by. These abrupt cuts in funding put that right at risk by undermining the humanitarian support and infrastructure that enables people around the world who have been forcibly displaced to access protection, placing already marginalized people in acute danger. We call on the U.S. government to restore funding immediately.”

a645.speaker: Amanda Klasing, national director of government relations and advocacy with Amnesty International USA
a645.name: Amanda Klasing
a645.title: national director of government relations and advocacy with Amnesty International USA
a645.speech: “It is a false choice that the U.S. government has to choose between addressing the economic needs of Americans or the rising cost of living here in the U.S. and development and humanitarian assistance abroad. Foreign assistance represents about one percent of the U.S. budget, and the U.S. has a global responsibility and interest in providing support to the most marginalized. As one of the world’s wealthiest nations with a history of providing the largest amount of foreign assistance, our analysis shows that this chaotic withdrawal from multilateral cooperation is in practice cruel and endangers the lives and rights of millions of people, especially people like women and girls in Afghanistan or refugees on the border of Thailand and Myanmar, children survivors of sexual violence in Haiti, and other marginalized populations already facing crisis. The U.S. government can – and must – do better.”

a645.speaker: Amnesty International (recommendations)
a645.name: Amnesty International (recommendations)
a645.speech: urges the Trump administration to restore foreign assistance, through the waiver process or otherwise, to programs where the chaotic and abrupt cut in funding has harmed human rights and ensure that future aid is administered consistent with human rights law and standards ; calls on Congress to continue robust funding of foreign assistance and reject any requests by the administration to codify foreign assistance cuts through rescission, and to use all available oversight levers ; says the Trump administration and Congress should work together to ensure that any changes to foreign assistance are carried out transparently, in consultation with affected communities, civil society, and international partners, and comply with international human rights law ; says all states in a position to do so should fulfill their obligations under UN General Assembly Resolution 2626 by committing at least 0.7% of gross national income to overseas aid without discrimination, and that donor states should increase support where possible to help fill critical funding gaps left by the abrupt U.S. aid suspensions.

a645.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order ‘Reevaluating and Realigning United States Foreign Aid’, January 20, 2025)
a645.name: Donald Trump
a645.title: US President (executive order ‘Reevaluating and Realigning United States Foreign Aid’, January 20, 2025)
a645.speech: issued the executive order under which the cuts have come, as well as other executive orders that targeted specific groups and programs for cuts.

a687.speaker: Paul Yaw Boateng, member of the House of Lords of the United Kingdom
a687.name: Paul Yaw Boateng
a687.title: member of the House of Lords of the United Kingdom
a687.speech: Has underscored the pivotal role of higher educational institutions, such as universities, in fostering leadership that is both innovative and service-oriented; lauded the critical role of academia in shaping leaders amid global challenges and reiterated that leadership and learning were indispensable to each other ; "So, institutions of higher education like this one, therefore, have a critical role to play in producing and shaping leaders and informing the actions of leadership" ; "Evidence based, cost policy and for the scale of the problems our world faces at this time, and the complexity of the nature the multi-faceted nature of effective action required to address them demands a response that is based not on rhetoric alone."

a687.speaker: Paul Yaw Boateng, member of the House of Lords of the United Kingdom
a687.name: Paul Yaw Boateng
a687.title: member of the House of Lords of the United Kingdom
a687.speech: On Ghana's economy, said it was high time the country moved away from reliance on foreign aid; adding that Ghana would not experience any significant growth since the dependence on external aid hindered progress.

a775.speaker: Christian Delmotte, President of Eurocham (European Chamber of Commerce in Cote d'Ivoire)
a775.name: Christian Delmotte
a775.title: President of Eurocham (European Chamber of Commerce in Cote d'Ivoire)
a775.speech: Stated that good governance is the pillar of economic growth and of corporate social responsibility in Cote d'Ivoire: "This programme, financed by Eurocham in collaboration with Siemens and the World Bank, was therefore designed to raise awareness among and train about one hundred Ivorian companies in adopting and implementing high standards of ethics, good governance and the fight against corruption" ; "Since its launch, the ACCG has made it possible to support some sixty companies, thereby contributing to a more ethical and transparent business environment in Cote d'Ivoire."

a775.speaker: Dr Franck Eba, Regional ESG manager at Hummingbird, and Fabrice Piofret, CEO of Veilleur des medias (panellists)
a775.name: Dr Franck Eba
a775.title: Regional ESG manager at Hummingbird, and Fabrice Piofret, CEO of Veilleur des medias (panellists)
a775.speech: Shared their experience in matters of ethics and good governance and above all what the programme brought them, in particular regarding internal control mechanisms and the importance of transparency in financial reporting.

a849.speaker: Global Water Partnership Organisation (statement on the GWPO website)
a849.name: Global Water Partnership Organisation (statement on the GWPO website)
a849.speech: "GWP faces an evolving international context, with shifting foreign aid priorities and increasing engagement from emerging economies. Alex will steer the organisation and improve the necessary governance protocols to embrace this new reality, exploring fresh partnerships and funding opportunities with nations and institutions that share GWP's vision of a water secure world" ; According to the statement, Alex will lead the establishment of GWPO regional hubs that, together with GWP Regional Water Partnerships, will serve as engines of a bold transformative agenda on integrated investments in water security and climate resilience ; "This shift aims to better serve our regions and also bring us closer to our country partners facing increased water risks and challenges."

a849.speaker: Global Water Partnership Organisation (statement)
a849.name: Global Water Partnership Organisation (statement)
a849.speech: "He has a proven track record of working with Heads of States, global and business leaders, in mobilising investments at scale. He pioneered the establishment of the first-ever International High-Level Panel on Water Investments for Africa, comprising 20 sitting and former Heads of State, and global leaders. Alex spearheaded support to the African Union (AU) in the development of the Continental Africa Water Investment Programme (AIP), which the Panel supports in its aim to close the water investment gap in Africa by mobilising $30 billion annually by 2030."

a849.speaker: Ban Ki-Moon, 8th UN Secretary-General
a849.name: Ban Ki-Moon
a849.title: 8th UN Secretary-General
a849.speech: In July 2023 commended the AIP's transformative approach and called on global leaders and international organisations to scale up the AIP globally.

a849.speaker: Pablo Bereciartua, Chair of GWP's Steering Committee
a849.name: Pablo Bereciartua
a849.title: Chair of GWP's Steering Committee
a849.speech: "We are pleased to have Alex lead GWP during this dynamic phase full of opportunities. His ability to build partnerships, mobilise resources, and lead diverse teams makes him the ideal person to drive GWP's vision and mission of water security for all. As GWP strengthens its network, develops new ways to grow its resources, and increases its regional impact, we are confident that Alex's leadership will amplify our global reach."

a849.speaker: António Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a849.name: António Guterres
a849.title: UN Secretary-General
a849.speech: Named the AIP as one of the key game-changing initiatives and commitments of the UN Water Action Agenda, aimed at driving transformation from a global water crisis to a water-secure world.

a849.speaker: Jakaya Kikwete, former President of the United Republic of Tanzania and Chair of the Board for GWP Southern Africa
a849.name: Jakaya Kikwete
a849.title: former President of the United Republic of Tanzania and Chair of the Board for GWP Southern Africa
a849.speech: Welcomed the GWP Steering Committee decision as 'a wise decision', and applauded his leadership abilities stating that: "Mr Simalabwi has been an exemplary GWPSA Executive Secretary and CEO - a visionary, diligent, and hands-on leader whose contributions have significantly advanced GWPSA's mission".

a849.speaker: Alex Simalabwi, incoming GWP Executive Secretary and CEO
a849.name: Alex Simalabwi
a849.title: incoming GWP Executive Secretary and CEO
a849.speech: "I am honoured to take on this role at such a pivotal time. For over two decades, GWP has been at the forefront of integrated water resources management. Now is the right time to change the status quo - pushed by the new global political dynamics and opening of new opportunities - and build on this strong foundation of GWP for bigger and stronger impacts, with unprecedented acceleration in both the pace and scale of mobilisation of climate-resilient water investments, in response to the current global water and climate emergency. I welcome the opportunity to join hands with global leaders and partners to lead the step-change of GWP into a transformative partner of choice for climate-resilient water investments. In the words of Nelson Mandela, 'it always seems impossible until it is done.'"

a939.speaker: Dr. Ashkir Nuur Qodax, member of the Darood delegation
a939.name: Dr. Ashkir Nuur Qodax
a939.title: member of the Darood delegation
a939.speech: First pointed out the importance of strengthening relations, saying that Egypt is a country of great importance to Somalia and that it is necessary to remember Egypt's past assistance to Somalia.

a939.speaker: Ahmed Qablan, delegation member from Kuwait
a939.name: Ahmed Qablan
a939.title: delegation member from Kuwait
a939.speech: Noted that this gathering of the Uqayliyiin is a forum in which people of one and the same lineage have come together.

a939.speaker: Dr. Abdirisaaq Muuse Barre, member of the Darood delegation
a939.name: Dr. Abdirisaaq Muuse Barre
a939.title: member of the Darood delegation
a939.speech: Elaborated on the importance of the relationship between the two clans that share a common ancestry, and said “that the occasion of this meeting is a historic one, and that it comes at a particularly important time.”

a939.speaker: Boqor Burhaan Boqor Muuse, King of the Darood
a939.name: Boqor Burhaan Boqor Muuse
a939.title: King of the Darood
a939.speech: Delivered an address that dwelt at length on the long-standing ties of the descendants of the Uqayliyiin, noting that today's meeting is historic and has come at its proper time; said that Egypt is a country that is a sister to Somalia and a pillar for the Islamic nation; concluded: “I hereby announce here the establishment of committees that will work on connection, the writing of history, cooperation and the elevation of relations between the two sides.”

a960.speaker: Tega Shiimi ya Shiimi, chief executive officer of Sanlam Investments
a960.name: Tega Shiimi ya Shiimi
a960.title: chief executive officer of Sanlam Investments
a960.speech: “His proposed tariffs on imports could reduce demand for Southern African exports and threaten the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), which supports trade with African nations. Additionally, Trump’s focus on domestic manufacturing may lead to reduced foreign investment in the region, further complicating economic relations.” ; noted Namibia may face significant challenges under Trump’s renewed presidency, specifically due to his “America First” policies that could lead to reduced US foreign aid, impacting health and infrastructure projects vital for Namibia’s development ; “Trump’s scepticism towards multilateral climate agreements threatens funding for environmental resilience initiatives, which are crucial for Namibia. Additionally, potential cuts to the AGOA could jeopardise trade benefits, affecting Namibia’s exports of beef, diamonds, and uranium. Conversely, there may be opportunities for increased trade partnerships if Namibia strategically positions itself in a competitive US-China landscape.”

a960.speaker: Senior Namibian government official (anonymous)
a960.name: Senior Namibian government official (anonymous)
a960.speech: noted Trump’s policies could result in Namibia being caught between South Africa and the USA in terms of AGOA: “Our ports could end up being the saving grace for South African exports to the USA depending on what extra conditions could be imposed by South Africa. As for tariffs, the Trump regime is just following the Biden regime in terms of targeting Chinese products such as electric vehicles or stopping key technologies the Chinese would want to get from the USA to their factories. But the jury is still deliberating on whether they will succeed.” ; added that Namibia is most likely, based on Trump’s first term, to see some rather benign, as opposed to increased support, in development aid, climate change mitigation and public health: “In Trump’s previous term, there was also more emphasis on bilateral trade frameworks as opposed to multilateral frameworks. Such an approach is normally not good for us who depend on the export of raw minerals and agricultural goods.”

a960.speaker: World Bank
a960.name: World Bank
a960.speech: has cautioned that Trump’s proposed trade tariffs could potentially have worldwide economic consequences ; expects the global economy to flatline at 2.7% growth during 2025 in response to fresh fears, including new US tariffs ; said even a 10% increase in US tariffs on imports from every country would reduce global economic growth by 0.2% if countries did not retaliate.

a960.speaker: Ayhan Kose, World Bank deputy chief economist
a960.name: Ayhan Kose
a960.title: World Bank deputy chief economist
a960.speech: said this global growth rate is one the bank can “live with” but would not be enough to improve living standards in richer and poorer countries; in a recent statement, Kose noted that “escalating trade tensions between major economies” were one of the bank’s biggest fears for the global economy in 2025 ; “Anytime you introduce restrictions on trade, there will be adverse consequences which are most often endured by the country that introduced them” ; “When you look over a longer time period, we think growth numbers will come down. That worries us” ; further warned there are no magic solutions for governments around the world grappling with different methods of boosting economic growth.

a960.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a960.name: Donald Trump
a960.title: US President
a960.speech: He threatened to impose higher tariffs on China, Canada, and Mexico on the first day of his presidency.

a998.speaker: A senior security operative / security source (anonymous)
a998.name: A senior security operative / security source (anonymous)
a998.speech: Told SaharaReporters that some youths from Buni Yadi, Gujba Local Government Area, killed two sons of a policeman attached to a station in the community, aged 20 and 13, when armed youths allegedly supported by the policeman’s colleagues invaded his house around 2am on Monday, March 17, 2025, also setting the house ablaze; and said the policeman was accused of being hard on "indigenes arrested for criminal activities" because he is from the Southern part of the country. "I swear to Allah, sir. It's so unfortunate. He (policeman) is very hardworking. But they accused him of being from the Southern part of the country and he should go and fight crime in his domain." ; "The incident occurred last week in Buni Yadi. The town, Buni Yadi, was once captured by Boko Haram for over five years. Although Boko Haram used to attack the town twice a month or more, employing hit-and-run tactics, the recent attack was different. A group of youths planned to kill a policeman in his home in Buni Yadi. The man I told you about earlier. Fortunately, he escaped, but unfortunately, they slaughtered his two children, aged 13 and 20. Initially, everyone thought Boko Haram was responsible, but an intelligence report has now come to light that some of his colleagues who are policemen at the police station in Buni Yadi, and some youths were behind the attack. Those in charge have the report already, which is why I don't want to mention names now. Our society is deteriorating. Meanwhile, the police house was burned down after the killing of his two sons. I reached out recently to him, and he told me he has left Yobe for his hometown."

a998.speaker: SP Dungus Abdulkarim, Yobe police command spokesperson (non-response)
a998.name: SP Dungus Abdulkarim
a998.title: Yobe police command spokesperson (non-response)
a998.speech: Calls made by SaharaReporters were not picked up nor returned, and a text message sent to his line was yet to be replied to as of the time of this report.

a1210.speaker: Abdoulie Sanyang, Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.name: Abdoulie Sanyang
a1210.title: Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.speech: Began by extending his deepest gratitude to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and the Executive Committee, for the opportunity to address the gathering. "This year's meeting comes at a critical time when global cooperation on refugee protection and humanitarian assistance is more essential than ever," ; adding that The Gambia like many other nations, has faced challenges, but has also triumphed in its efforts to safeguard the dignity and rights of refugees, asylum seekers and stateless persons.

a1210.speaker: Abdoulie Sanyang, Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.name: Abdoulie Sanyang
a1210.title: Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.speech: "Despite our limited resources, we have remained steadfast in our commitment to provide refuge to those fleeing conflict, persecution, and natural disasters. The Gambia has a long tradition of hospitality, guided by principles of humanitarian practices and solidarity with our brothers and sisters across the continent." ; "Our national systems including healthcare, education, and social services, are under strain. The Gambia, although small in size, has played its part in responding to these global crises. We have welcomed over 4,200 refugees from 21 countries ensuring that they find safety, security, and inclusion."

a1210.speaker: Abdoulie Sanyang, Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.name: Abdoulie Sanyang
a1210.title: Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.speech: Noted that the world is witnessing unprecedented levels of forced displacement, and said conflicts in neighbouring regions, economic instability, irregular and clandestine migrations, and climate change-led migration, are exacerbating vulnerabilities that are pushing millions to seek refuge across borders ; further stated that rising sea levels and erratic weather patterns are threatening livelihoods, forcing communities to migrate ; also expounded on the global economic downturn and the effects of climate change which he said has further complicated the ability to extend protection and humanitarian assistance to refugees.

a1210.speaker: Abdoulie Sanyang, Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.name: Abdoulie Sanyang
a1210.title: Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.speech: "Hence, international solidarity and burden-sharing are crucial. I stand with the international community in reinforcing support for hosting refugees, particularly in the Gambia, where resources are often scarce. The Gambia is also committed to addressing the root causes of displacement, missing persons, and irregular migration. Through active engagement in regional peace-building efforts, we strive to contribute to the resolution of conflicts that force people to flee their homes. Our involvement in the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) peacekeeping missions is a testament to our commitment to ensure stability in the sub-region," adding that The Gambia further calls for more robust global action on climate change including climate finance mechanisms that support adaptation and resilience-building for developing countries.

a1210.speaker: Abdoulie Sanyang, Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.name: Abdoulie Sanyang
a1210.title: Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.speech: "While we have made progress, we cannot overlook the urgent need for more durable solutions for refugees. The Gambia is working closely with the UNHCR to strengthen resettlement, voluntary repatriation, and local integration programs. We believe that refugees should be empowered to rebuild their lives and contribute to their host communities. We must all work together to create opportunities for them to thrive through education, vocational training, and employment."

a1210.speaker: Abdoulie Sanyang, Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.name: Abdoulie Sanyang
a1210.title: Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.speech: Commended the UNHCR for their unwavering dedication and tireless work in protecting the rights of refugees worldwide. "Your efforts continue to bring hope to millions who have been displaced and on the move. Being stateless and being a refugee is not a choice you make."

a1210.speaker: Abdoulie Sanyang, Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.name: Abdoulie Sanyang
a1210.title: Gambia's Interior Minister
a1210.speech: In his conclusion, he reaffirmed The Gambia's commitment to uphold international refugee laws, as well as to ensure that refugees and displaced persons are treated with dignity and respect. He equally emphasised the importance of strong international cooperation, shared responsibility, and genuine solidarity to mitigate the challenges faced. "Let us move forward together, united in our pursuit of a more just, inclusive, and compassionate world for all."

a1255.speaker: Bulisa Mbano, corporate rescue practitioner of Khayah Cement
a1255.name: Bulisa Mbano
a1255.title: corporate rescue practitioner of Khayah Cement
a1255.speech: "The meeting went on well and it is our hope that the resolutions for the rescue plan will be implemented in accordance with our time lines for the befit of investors and creditors," he said. ; "It is our hope that what we have managed to gather today will set the tone towards the revival of the entity." ; "Of course, there are challenges, but engagements are key in finding each other and get to real issues for the revival of the entity."

a1266.speaker: Leaders at the 8th African Leadership Forum (ALF)
a1266.name: Leaders at the 8th African Leadership Forum (ALF)
a1266.speech: Have urged the continent to seize the moment and create new conditions that can enable an 'Africa first' in efforts to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

a1266.speaker: Yoweri Museveni, President of Uganda
a1266.name: Yoweri Museveni
a1266.title: President of Uganda
a1266.speech: Opening the Forum, made reference to the SDGs by breaking them down as aimed at removing strategic bottlenecks that block socio economic transformation across the continent. He noted that for countries to head towards transformation, they have to start from the basic level of building strong, capable states with good policies built around national interests. In their case, he said their economy had been built in 5 stages since they started running government, in the form of minimum recovery, expanding the old colonial economy, diversifying the economy, value addition into the economy and moving towards a knowledge economy.

a1266.speaker: Dr. Jakaya Mrisho Kikwete, ALF 2025 convener, ALF Patron and fourth President of the United Republic of Tanzania
a1266.name: Dr. Jakaya Mrisho Kikwete
a1266.title: ALF 2025 convener, ALF Patron and fourth President of the United Republic of Tanzania
a1266.speech: Noted that in resetting SDGs implementation on the right path, urgency of action could not be overstated with high political will and turning ambition into action. He noted that despite there being challenges in the implementation, that should be changed into opportunity and reaffirm local commitment to SDGs and Africa Agenda 2030. He also called for prioritizing of economic growth which then produces jobs and an education that is able to create world class learning outcomes and a middle class.

a1266.speaker: H.E. Hailemariam Desalegn, ALF co-convener and former Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
a1266.name: H.E. Hailemariam Desalegn
a1266.title: ALF co-convener and former Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
a1266.speech: Noted that Africa faces opportunities but with challenges in achieving SDGs, such as a huge funding gap and thus significant resources needed to fill the gap. He also proposed alternatives to funding the SDGs while calling for solutions like strengthened governance and institutions, transparency, rule of law, combatting corruption and curbing illicit financial flows, alongside a resilient workforce, sustainable food security, reliable energy and strengthening of integration in trade and the broader economies across the continent through ceding some of individual countries' sovereignty and embracing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). "If it gets harder to trade with other more established economies in the west, its only prudent that we strengthen intra trade, leverage technology and innovation, resource mobilise and cur on foreign aid and Overseas Development Assistance (ODA)."

a1266.speaker: Antonio Pedro, Deputy Executive Secretary at the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa
a1266.name: Antonio Pedro
a1266.title: Deputy Executive Secretary at the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa
a1266.speech: Noted that in implementing SDGs, it was important to understand that unemployment is not merely an economic concern but also a threat to peace and a test to our economic model, adding that private sector must not just invest in profit but also in purpose. He argued that the continent needed a recalibrated SDG model, further noting that removing tariff and non-tariff barriers has the potential to increase Africa's intra trade by 45 per cent in the next decade.

a1266.speaker: Mafa Chipeta, former FAO representative to Ethiopia, the African Union and UNECA, FAO Subregional Coordinator for Eastern Africa
a1266.name: Mafa Chipeta
a1266.title: former FAO representative to Ethiopia, the African Union and UNECA, FAO Subregional Coordinator for Eastern Africa
a1266.speech: In a keynote statement, argued for an approach that is more selective and re-focused in implementation, noting that if the continent takes on all the SDGs at one go, it may spread itself too thin. The basis of his argument was hinged on the facts that the continent has 17 to 18 percent of global population but with just 2 percent of the World GDP and trade, scores 3 percent for most economic indices and with only less than 0.5 percent for new critical technologies. He further cautioned that African trade ministries tend to ignore the larger domestic trade than foreign trade which leaves exploitative traders to rob smallholders and continues to heavily subsidise the world economy by selling raw, unprocessed low value materials cheaply and buys the same back at inflated prices. He proposed that the continent needs to cut down on donor dependency by still allocating its own funds so that donors don't replace local commitment.

a1266.speaker: Dr. Ernest Bai Koroma, former President of the Republic of Sierra Leone
a1266.name: Dr. Ernest Bai Koroma
a1266.title: former President of the Republic of Sierra Leone
a1266.speech: Noted that while the current 'America' first plan had created uncertainty in the rest of the world, it was also timely for Africa to grab this opportunity so that it re-anchors itself and make new bold decisions in new development directions. He urged prioritizing human capital development through education, health and social services delivery, agriculture development and good governance with leadership that is determined to drive all these processes.

a1266.speaker: Dr Mohamed Moncef Marzouki, former President of the Republic of Tunisia
a1266.name: Dr Mohamed Moncef Marzouki
a1266.title: former President of the Republic of Tunisia
a1266.speech: Called for Africa to rely on itself through intra trade, which should be preceded by having democratic, independent and corrupt free governments.

a1266.speaker: Gilbert Bukenya, former Vice President of Uganda
a1266.name: Gilbert Bukenya
a1266.title: former Vice President of Uganda
a1266.speech: Said Africa should have innovative leadership that circumvents those who want to manage it with external interests and instead drive its own agenda on transformation.

a1266.speaker: Sam Kutesa, retired Ugandan Foreign Affairs Minister
a1266.name: Sam Kutesa
a1266.title: retired Ugandan Foreign Affairs Minister
a1266.speech: Said the SDGs were proper aspirations and that what was needed for the continent is innovating new measures to finance their implementation, like leveraging local natural resources and private sector to finance them.

a1377.speaker: South Africa's National Treasury
a1377.name: South Africa's National Treasury
a1377.speech: Said Monday that the World Bank granted South Africa a $1.5 billion loan to upgrade transportation infrastructure and help it transition toward a low-carbon economy. "This agreement reinforces the strong and constructive collaboration between the World Bank and the government of South Africa." ; "This partnership marks a significant step toward addressing South Africa's pressing economic challenges of low growth and high unemployment." It added that because the financing has better conditions than conventional borrowing, such as a three-year grace period, it should reduce escalating debt-service expenses.

a1377.speaker: South African government
a1377.name: South African government
a1377.speech: While it did not give specifics, said it expects the World Bank loan will enable inclusive economic growth and job creation by assisting in the removal of important infrastructure bottlenecks, especially in the energy and freight transportation sectors.

a1377.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President, and his coalition government
a1377.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a1377.title: South African President, and his coalition government
a1377.speech: Have pledged to tackle corruption and decades of poor management as well as pursue reforms to get the country out of its economic rut and ease its extremely high unemployment rate.

a1377.speaker: Enoch Godongwana, Finance Minister of South Africa
a1377.name: Enoch Godongwana
a1377.title: Finance Minister of South Africa
a1377.speech: Said government debt is projected to stabilize at 77.4% of GDP in 2025/26.

a1377.speaker: Enoch Godongwana, Finance Minister of South Africa
a1377.name: Enoch Godongwana
a1377.title: Finance Minister of South Africa
a1377.speech: Said the country doesn't have the funds to cover the more than $430 million shortfall caused by the Trump administration's cuts in foreign aid, which have threatened the vast network of support for one of the world's largest HIV-positive populations.

a1707.speaker: Mahmoud Mohieldin, World Bank Group Senior Vice President for the 2030 Development Agenda, and Svetlana Klimenko, Lead Financial Management Specialist at the World Bank Group (op-ed authors)
a1707.name: Mahmoud Mohieldin
a1707.title: World Bank Group Senior Vice President for the 2030 Development Agenda, and Svetlana Klimenko, Lead Financial Management Specialist at the World Bank Group (op-ed authors)
a1707.speech: Argue that the annual funding gap for the Sustainable Development Goals is many trillions of dollars and that "the only way to close that gap is with the help of the private sector - in particular, by impelling companies to account in their decision-making for environmental, social, and governance issues relevant to the SDGs" ; note that at the latest United Nations High-Level Political Forum governments rolled out impressive blueprints "almost none of which included realistic budgets or revenue sources" ; argue that executives must balance attention to short-term performance with a long-term perspective, and that by creating smart, comprehensive, and clearly defined strategies private companies can help governments establish realistic budgets and clear financing plans for the SDGs.

a1707.speaker: 2016 Global Sustainable Investment Review (report)
a1707.name: 2016 Global Sustainable Investment Review (report)
a1707.speech: Reported that $22.89 trillion worth of assets were "being professionally managed under responsible investment strategies" worldwide, up 25% from 2014, with Europe accounting for $12 trillion and the US total at $8.7 trillion, though the highest growth rates were in Japan and Oceania.

a1707.speaker: Gianni Betti, Costanza Consolandi, and Robert G. Eccles (recent paper)
a1707.name: Gianni Betti
a1707.title: Costanza Consolandi, and Robert G. Eccles (recent paper)
a1707.speech: Map the relevant ESG issues identified by the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) in 79 industries in ten sectors, grouped by SDGs.

a1707.speaker: Mozaffar Khan, George Serafeim, and Aaron Yoon (2016 study)
a1707.name: Mozaffar Khan
a1707.title: George Serafeim, and Aaron Yoon (2016 study)
a1707.speech: Created portfolios of companies that were performing well and poorly on the material issues in their industry; the firms with the highest annualized active return (alpha) of 4.8% were performing well on the material issues and poorly on the immaterial issues, while those with the lowest alpha, -2.2%, were performing poorly on both, and the divergences did not start to appear until after 7-8 years.

a1841.speaker: World Bank
a1841.name: World Bank
a1841.speech: Emphasises the importance of a strong fiscal system by adopting fiscal rules, improving expenditure controls and promoting transparency through timely fiscal statistics and an independent Fiscal Council.

a1875.speaker: Julien Kpédji, executive director of the Organisation of Blind Women of Benin (Ofab)
a1875.name: Julien Kpédji
a1875.title: executive director of the Organisation of Blind Women of Benin (Ofab)
a1875.speech: presented the organisation and reviewed the major achievements completed or under way before finishing with the prospects. According to him, Ofab pursues objectives such as vocational training for girls and women with disabilities for economic self-sufficiency; literacy training for adult women with disabilities in order to strengthen their management capacity; the discouragement of all forms of gender-based and disability-related violence; and facilitating access to justice. He stated that Ofab has impacted several communities of people living with disabilities, notably through the reopening of and contribution to running the centre for the blind in Natitingou, the codification of literacy signs for Fongbé and related languages in Braille, and the transcription into Braille and Fongbé of reading and mathematics materials. He also mentioned women's financial empowerment, which financed income-generating activities for 27 visually impaired women, even though, he underlines, the project did not prosper for lack of follow-up. To conclude, he highlighted as prospects Ofab's gender policy together with a three-year action plan.

a1875.speaker: Technical and financial partners present at the meeting
a1875.name: Technical and financial partners present at the meeting
a1875.speech: welcomed the effort and the sacrifices made by Ofab and reiterated their support for the fulfilment of women and girls with disabilities.

a1875.speaker: Nicole Abouyo, Africa officer for the Making It Work (MIW) project of Handicap International
a1875.name: Nicole Abouyo
a1875.title: Africa officer for the Making It Work (MIW) project of Handicap International
a1875.speech: announced the imminent participation of the Coalition of Women with Disabilities of Benin, of which Ofab is a member, in the Beijing 2030 report that Benin will present. This initiative will ensure, for the first time in history, inclusive participation in favour of women with disabilities.

a1875.speaker: Jean-Claude Lodjo, technical adviser in leadership-management-accountability and governance, USAID representative
a1875.name: Jean-Claude Lodjo
a1875.title: technical adviser in leadership-management-accountability and governance, USAID representative
a1875.speech: expressed his interest in the initiative, an initiative to be supported all the more since, he specifies, USAID, through its Health Systems Strengthening project, has set up a private-sector support component for better accessibility to health services, with a prominent place for associations and businesses run by women or people living with disabilities.

a1886.speaker: Pamela Fessenden, USAID Mission Director
a1886.name: Pamela Fessenden
a1886.title: USAID Mission Director
a1886.speech: Speaking at the event, expressed appreciation for the strong working relationship between USAID and the two ministries. She highlighted some of the achievements of the partnership, including the development and printing of Standard 1-4 curriculum and instructional materials in both English and Chichewa, training of 24,000 Standard 1-2 teachers, and initiation of a revision of the Inclusive Education Strategy ; also noted the completion of 72 Community Day Secondary Schools (CDSS) and progress on 17 CDSS construction sites, which are currently at an average of 65 percent completion, and that the partnership developed induction standards for newly hired primary school teachers and teaching practice.

a1886.speaker: Dr. Levis Eneya, Secretary for Higher Education
a1886.name: Dr. Levis Eneya
a1886.title: Secretary for Higher Education
a1886.speech: Acknowledged USAID's contributions, noting their significant impact on the advancement of education in Malawi.

a1886.speaker: Dr. Rachel Chimbwete Phiri, Secretary for Basic and Secondary Education
a1886.name: Dr. Rachel Chimbwete Phiri
a1886.title: Secretary for Basic and Secondary Education
a1886.speech: Described the partnership as both beneficial and transformative.

a2125.speaker: Nabih Berri, Lebanese Parliament Speaker (statement from his press office)
a2125.name: Nabih Berri
a2125.title: Lebanese Parliament Speaker (statement from his press office)
a2125.speech: Asked the United Nations to "establish an airlift ensuring the delivery of humanitarian aid supplies." ; At the same time he called on the International Committee of the Red Cross and the Lebanese Red Crescent to "fulfil their duty", delivering food and medical supplies to the Lebanese of the south of the country, the area most affected by Israeli air strikes, along with Beirut.

a2125.speaker: Nabih Berri, Lebanese Parliament Speaker (statement from his press office)
a2125.name: Nabih Berri
a2125.title: Lebanese Parliament Speaker (statement from his press office)
a2125.speech: Thanked "all the brotherly and friendly Arab countries that immediately began sending aid", as well as the Lebanese people and all the political forces that took in the displaced people who had been "unjustly" targeted by Israel's "destruction machine."

a2125.speaker: Najib Mikati, caretaker Prime Minister of Lebanon
a2125.name: Najib Mikati
a2125.title: caretaker Prime Minister of Lebanon
a2125.speech: Warned that the country "is facing one of the most dangerous phases in its history", words that came hours after the Israeli army launched a new invasion of the country, after more than 11 months of fighting with Hezbollah on the border. ; Praised the "continuous support" of the UN and of "brotherly Arab countries and other friendly countries", and made an "urgent" appeal for more aid to "reinforce the ongoing efforts to provide basic assistance to the displaced."

a2125.speaker: United Nations
a2125.name: United Nations
a2125.speech: Appealed for around 426 million dollars (about 383 million euros) to help the roughly one million people displaced in Lebanon by Israel's attacks.

a2322.speaker: Dalitso Kabambe, UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2322.name: Dalitso Kabambe
a2322.title: UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2322.speech: "Chakweranomics has never worked for Malawians," he declared, accusing President Lazarus Chakwera of being out of touch with the reality facing Malawians and describing the current economic policies under Chakwera as a failure; argued that the government's reliance on foreign aid, rather than addressing fundamental issues such as foreign exchange shortages, fertilizer access, and food security, has only deepened the crisis.

a2322.speaker: Dalitso Kabambe, UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2322.name: Dalitso Kabambe
a2322.title: UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2322.speech: Contended that the President's call for continued aid in response to Malawi's growing fertilizer and food insecurity was misguided and insisted Chakwera should have taken decisive action to address the root causes: "Instead of asking for help, the President should have started by holding accountable those responsible for these crises and implementing robust economic policies to safeguard the nation's forex reserves."

a2322.speaker: Dalitso Kabambe, UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2322.name: Dalitso Kabambe
a2322.title: UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2322.speech: Criticised the Chakwera administration for failing to create an environment conducive to investment and said the President should have prioritized investments in key forex-generating sectors including mining, agriculture, and manufacturing: "The government should have been working to boost key sectors of the economy that could generate foreign currency and create jobs, not relying on begging bowls and short-term solutions."

a2322.speaker: Dalitso Kabambe, UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2322.name: Dalitso Kabambe
a2322.title: UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2322.speech: Argued that Chakwera should have moved to revive Admarc, the Agricultural Development and Marketing Corporation, to ensure farmers had access to necessary inputs and a sustainable market: "Instead of waiting for international aid, the government should be strengthening its own institutions that can support the farmers who are at the heart of the economy."

a2322.speaker: Dalitso Kabambe, UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2322.name: Dalitso Kabambe
a2322.title: UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2322.speech: Argued that the government's approach to fuel importation contradicts basic economic principles and exposes the country's vulnerability, claiming the fuel policy has further deepened the country's foreign exchange crisis, making essential imports even more difficult to secure.

a2322.speaker: Dalitso Kabambe, UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2322.name: Dalitso Kabambe
a2322.title: UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2322.speech: "It's been nearly three years since this administration took office, yet we see no real change for the better. People are suffering, and instead of addressing the real issues, the President is busy with speeches that offer no hope for the future."

a2322.speaker: Kondwani Nankhumwa, People's Development Party (PDP) president
a2322.name: Kondwani Nankhumwa
a2322.title: People's Development Party (PDP) president
a2322.speech: Described the President's recent national address as "empty" and devoid of any substantial plans for the country's recovery.

a2573.speaker: Industry assessments (cited)
a2573.name: Industry assessments (cited)
a2573.speech: According to industry assessments, delays at Ghana’s ports cost businesses an estimated $200 million annually in demurrage and storage fees, severely affecting trade flows and economic performance.

a2573.speaker: Organizers of the Ghana-International Shipping and Logistics Summit (Akwaabaa Communication and industry stakeholders)
a2573.name: Organizers of the Ghana-International Shipping and Logistics Summit (Akwaabaa Communication and industry stakeholders)
a2573.speech: “Despite the sector’s significant potential to drive trade, job creation, and industrial growth, it is being held back by deep-rooted inefficiencies” ; “We need a coordinated and transformative approach that fosters collaboration between government, private operators, and international partners.”

a2573.speaker: Organizers of the summit
a2573.name: Organizers of the summit
a2573.speech: Highlight that technology providers and digital innovators will play a central role in discussions, particularly around customs automation, cargo tracking, and data integration.

a2573.speaker: Organizers of the summit
a2573.name: Organizers of the summit
a2573.speech: Pointed to the urgent need for policy coherence and better access to financing, noting that many local logistics providers are unable to expand or innovate due to limited access to affordable credit, further entrenching inefficiencies and stifling growth.

a2660.speaker: Annika Jayawardenar, Head of Development Cooperation at the Swedish Embassy
a2660.name: Annika Jayawardenar
a2660.title: Head of Development Cooperation at the Swedish Embassy
a2660.speech: Said “protecting the rights of girls is key to sustaining social and economic development so learning how to uphold rights is vital,” as she signed a Grant Agreement with Kebour Ghenna, Executive Director of IA last Thursday.

a2660.speaker: Kebour Ghenna, Executive Director of Initiative Africa (IA)
a2660.name: Kebour Ghenna
a2660.title: Executive Director of Initiative Africa (IA)
a2660.speech: During the ceremony, Kebour pointed out that empowerment projects such as this one are geared towards helping young girls and women have a voice in the society and achieve their full potential. Kebour appreciated the Swedish Embassy for the support it lent to the organization since 2006.

a2696.speaker: Trump administration
a2696.name: Trump administration
a2696.speech: Has expressed interest in promoting health initiatives focused on economic growth and self-reliance in developing countries.

a2702.speaker: President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce and the interim USAID representative (jointly)
a2702.name: President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce and the interim USAID representative (jointly)
a2702.speech: Pleaded before the business community: "This state of affairs must change and women must find their place in these male trades."

a2702.speaker: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a2702.name: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh
a2702.title: President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a2702.speech: "This workshop is crucial because it will make it possible to raise awareness and inform the private sector about the importance of integrating women into the trades of logistics, construction and transport, a professional environment that has been predominantly male until now." ; Recalled the results of the preliminary "gender" assessment carried out by the Education Development Center (EDC) team in March 2017 ; Launched an appeal to the business community to "work together in order to find rapid and lasting solutions and thus remove the obstacles to the recruitment of women and, ultimately, contribute to the country's economic development," describing it as an "initiative fully in line with the will of the Head of State to highlight the role of women in Djiboutian society and to combat unemployment and discrimination against them" ; Recalled that the awareness-raising workshop bringing together representatives of the construction, logistics and transport sectors should be the ideal moment to solve this problem.

a2702.speaker: Education Development Center (EDC), preliminary gender assessment of March 2017
a2702.name: Education Development Center (EDC)
a2702.title: preliminary gender assessment of March 2017
a2702.speech: Identified all the obstacles, such as cultural norms, that prevent young women coming out of vocational training institutions from accessing these technical fields.

a2702.speaker: Alpha Diallo, interim USAID representative in Djibouti
a2702.name: Alpha Diallo
a2702.title: interim USAID representative in Djibouti
a2702.speech: Insisted on the value of the meeting as an opportunity to reverse an over-unbalanced trend and return to fairness and gender equality, and on the importance of raising awareness on the gender question, which stems from the inequality of social relations between men and women ; Paid tribute to the efforts of the Djiboutian government, which has "strengthened the status, the position and the capacities of women in several fields" ; Deplored the gender-based inequalities that women continue to suffer disproportionately, such as the burden of poverty, illiteracy and above all poor access to resources and economic opportunities ; "Young women who do manage to find a job in technical fields often risk being victims of gender-based discrimination in their workplace."

a2702.speaker: Alpha Diallo, interim USAID representative in Djibouti
a2702.name: Alpha Diallo
a2702.title: interim USAID representative in Djibouti
a2702.speech: Said he wanted to believe in "the legislative and regulatory arsenal which stipulates equality of opportunity between the sexes in terms of education, training, employment and pay"; according to him the American international cooperation agency "attaches capital importance to the gender question and recognises it as a development issue," and the gender question will be addressed in the implementation of the activities of the Djibouti Employability Project ; Recalled that this awareness-raising workshop follows a previous similar meeting that served to interest and awaken teachers and administrators of technical and vocational education to the theme of gender in training streams.

a2702.speaker: Zahra Youssouf Kayad, former Secretary of State for National Solidarity and coordinator of the Djibouti Employability Project
a2702.name: Zahra Youssouf Kayad
a2702.title: former Secretary of State for National Solidarity and coordinator of the Djibouti Employability Project
a2702.speech: Gave a broad presentation on the problems related to women and their difficulties in entering certain trades and even specialised markets.

a2977.speaker: UK-Malawi Chamber of Commerce (UK-MCC) (statement)
a2977.name: UK-Malawi Chamber of Commerce (UK-MCC) (statement)
a2977.speech: Says the launch has been organised in partnership with the Scotland Malawi Partnership and in collaboration with the office of the Malawi High Commission to the UK ; “This milestone occasion will bring together Scottish and Malawian business leaders, diaspora entrepreneurs, development partners, and government officials to celebrate and strengthen bilateral trade and investment relationships” ; It adds that the UK-MCC “is an apolitical, member-led organisation that operates independently to promote trade and investment” and that “it receives support from both Malawi Government and the Government of the United Kingdom — in this case the Scottish Government” ; According to UK-MCC, the partnership reinforces the body’s position “as a reliable platform for collaborative economic development”, adding that Mumba’s presence “underscores Malawi Government’s strong commitment to promoting economic diplomacy, attracting foreign direct investment, and building sustainable international partnerships”.

a2977.speaker: Dr Thomas Bisika, Malawi’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom and UK-MCC Patron
a2977.name: Dr Thomas Bisika
a2977.title: Malawi’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom and UK-MCC Patron
a2977.speech: “Malawi is ready for business. As we aspire to become an upper middle-income and self-reliant country, it is clear that trade and investment will be important. The UK Malawi Chamber of Commerce is well positioned to support UK businesses planning to invest in Malawi. The launch of the Scotland Chapter will add impetus to Malawi’s quest for increased Foreign Direct Investment (FDI).”

a2977.speaker: Organisers of the launch (UK-MCC)
a2977.name: Organisers of the launch (UK-MCC)
a2977.speech: Say the event will be moderated by UK-MCC chief executive officer, Hannington Gondwe, whose confirmed speakers include Minister Mumba; H.E. Dr Bisika and Edgar Chibaka, who is chairperson and co-founder of UK-MCC & first response group; other speakers are Tracy Mitchell, Managing Director for True Origin; Robert Anderson, Managing Director for African Lakes Company; Louise Davies, Chief Executive for Scottish Fair Trade; Cameron McAllister, Director for MF Coffee — “with more speakers to be announced later” ; Added that the UK-MCC Scotland Chapter is set to serve as “a vital platform to support market access, investment readiness, policy dialogue, and sustainable trade partnerships”, and “With growing interest in priority sectors such as agro-processing, renewable energy, manufacturing and tourism, Malawi offers vast potential for inclusive growth”, adding that registration is required as spaces are limited.

a2977.speaker: Edgar Chibaka, UK-MCC chairperson and co-founder
a2977.name: Edgar Chibaka
a2977.title: UK-MCC chairperson and co-founder
a2977.speech: “This is a defining moment for Malawi–Scotland relations. We are excited to welcome Hon. Mumba and other distinguished guests to Edinburgh. The Scotland Chapter represents our commitment to enabling trade through diaspora-led structures and building a new era of economic collaboration,” he said, while inviting businesses, investors, and changemakers “to be part of this transformative journey”.

a2977.speaker: Stuart Brown, CEO of the Scotland Malawi Partnership
a2977.name: Stuart Brown
a2977.title: CEO of the Scotland Malawi Partnership
a2977.speech: “This launch represents a natural evolution of the deep people-to-people links that Scotland and Malawi have built over generations. We’re proud to support this initiative, which brings economic opportunity into the heart of that partnership. It’s about promoting fair, ethical, and inclusive trade that benefits both nations — and creating new connections that will last long into the future.”

a3112.speaker: Lieutenant General Oscar Nyoni, commander of the Zambian Air Force and host of the symposium
a3112.name: Lieutenant General Oscar Nyoni
a3112.title: commander of the Zambian Air Force and host of the symposium
a3112.speech: “We are focusing on humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, because these two areas are among the worst enemies of the continent’s development.”

a3112.speaker: General James B. Hecker, commander of USAFE-AFAFRICA
a3112.name: General James B. Hecker
a3112.title: commander of USAFE-AFAFRICA
